## FILE: `README.md`

# Etched in Schema

**An identity that acts — and can prove what it did.**

Etched in Schema is a self-contained 3tched identity — the living embodiment
of a business subsidiary — that turns a business goal into deployed,
working infrastructure. Every action it takes is authorised against its
capabilities, bounded by compliance rules, recorded as a tamper-evident
receipt, and anchored on a blockchain so anyone can verify *who did what,
under what authority, and what actually happened* without trusting the agent
or its operator.

Built for the Meta Model API hackathon (Startup Track — judged on a working
product) by Jeremy Hobson, founder of 3tched.

## Why

AI agents can reason about goals, but they rarely have a durable identity,
verifiable permissions, accountable execution, or the ability to build and
operate real systems. On-chain artifacts have the mirror-image problem: a
contract address or a content hash proves something exists, not that it came
from an accountable actor following permitted steps. That missing link
between artifacts and accountable, authorised actors is what keeps businesses
from trusting both autonomous agents and Web3.

Etched in Schema closes that gap from both sides: every on-chain artifact
points to the identity and authorised operation behind it, and every
operation points to the artifacts it produced, with the history anchored
on-chain.

## Goals — the new, judged product

The identity platform (3tched) existed before the hackathon and is used only
through its interfaces. The **new development, built and judged here**, is:

1. **Compliance routing** — a business's requirements become an OSCAL profile;
   OSCAL tags route each request and each requirement to the components and
   plugin operations that implement it.
2. **Rule enforcement** — boundary rules compile into the capability grants,
   budgets and network policy that are enforced on every call, with a clear
   refusal (and the exact missing capability) when a request is out of bounds.
3. **Policy** — authoring, versioning and evaluating the rules: what each
   identity may do, which actions need human approval (two approvals for root),
   and what happens to data (e.g. PII redaction, retention).
4. **Drop-in consumer app** — the existing UI generator repurposed: one spec
   renders on the web and in tools people already use, starting with **team chat** — an open-source
   Matrix client (Element) first, reaching other chat tools through Matrix
   bridges — and every action is governed by 1–3. Spec:
   [docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md](docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md).
   A user asks in team chat; the request is routed, checked against policy,
   executed through the identity or refused, and the receipt comes back in the
   thread.

The web UI is optional, only if time allows.

**Golden path** (a working product, end to end, three times in a row before
anything else): a user asks the agent in team chat to do something for a business
→ compliance routing maps it to the required controls and operations →
policy is evaluated → allowed operations run through the identity and return
receipts; a disallowed one is refused with the reason → the thread shows the
result, the receipts, and any redaction applied.

Out of the critical path: the avatar/embodiment, moving identities between
hosts, client acquisition, and on-chain anchoring (kept only if it fits once
the golden path works).

## What is new vs. what already exists

Everything in **this repository** is developed during the hackathon. It is
built *on* 3tched, which already exists and is used only through its
published interfaces (see [docs/3TCHED-RESOURCES.md](docs/3TCHED-RESOURCES.md)).

| New in this repo (judged) | Existing 3tched resource it uses |
|---|---|
| OSCAL catalog of 3tched capabilities, tag taxonomy, profiles, component definitions | `oscal_subid_registry` (subid discovery), `schema_tag_registry` (tag metadata, owner-scoped policy) |
| Compliance router: request / profile → controls → plugin operations | sealed plugin catalog, identity operation files (3tchedFS) |
| Rule enforcement: OSCAL rules → capability grants, budgets, OpenFlow policy; refusals with reasons | bridge per-call capability check, `openflow` / `ovsdb_bridge`, router budgets |
| Policy engine and policy documents (approvals, redaction, retention) | `schema_tag_registry` policies, `routing_decision`, `elevation` |
| Drop-in consumer app: team chat first (Matrix/Element) | chat path to Meta's model, identity receipts |
| Business declarations (starting with a Florida LLC) | — |

Pre-existing and **not** part of the judged work: the identity container and
sled, kernel-peer admission, 3tchedFS, the bridge and MutationEngine, receipts,
the router, and the 3tched.com UI.

## Architecture at a glance

```
          internet only                      local filesystem only
  Meta model API  ◄──┐                 ┌──► 3tchedFS mount (lungs) ──► 3tched bridge
  blockchain      ◄──┤   IDENTITY      │      kernel-peer identity, capability check,
                     └── CONTAINER  ───┘      MutationEngine commit, receipt
                          (the twin)
                               │
            OSCAL profile ─► tag router ─► plugin operations (incus, openflow, …)
                               │
                  receipts ─► Web3 index ─► Merkle root anchored on-chain
```

- The identity has **no network path to 3tched**; it reaches 3tched only
  through its own FUSE mount, where every operation is a typed file.
- Its only network is the internet: the Meta model API and the blockchain.
- Subsidiaries map to Linux users; the root is the 3tched control plane.
  See [docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md](docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md).
- How this compares to SPIFFE, BeyondCorp and DIDs, and what it adds:
  [docs/PRIOR-ART.md](docs/PRIOR-ART.md).

## FILE: `docs/DROP-IN-SPEC.md`

# Drop-in spec: one generator, every surface

The drop-in is the existing 3tched UI generator, repurposed: the same spec
pipeline that renders the web UI also renders into consumer apps (team chat
first), and every action it exposes is governed by the new compliance
routing, policy and enforcement.

Marked **existing** (3tched today, used through its interfaces) or **new**
(built and judged in this repository).

## 1. What the generator does today (existing)

| Capability | Where it lives |
|---|---|
| **Catalog**: the components a UI may use, as sealed declarations (Canvas profile, whole-application contract, imported shadcn component schemas) | `json_render` plugin: `list_catalog`, `list_components`, `get_component_schema`, `get_catalog_entry` |
| **Spec**: a json-render element tree, validated against the catalog | `json_render`: `get_spec_schema`, `validate_spec`, `export_json_schema` |
| **Generation**: the model is given the catalog surface and writes a spec; the spec is validated before rendering | `json_render`: `build_prompt_surface`; chat application mode (`json_render_generation`) |
| **Deterministic rendering**: a UI built directly from a plugin's sealed schema, no model involved | `schema_renderer`: `render_schema`, `get_rendering`, `validate_schema`, `list_galleries` |
| **Gallery**: specs a human kept, saved as candidates and promoted into catalog entries | `json_render`: `save_candidate`, `list_candidates`, `promote_candidate`, `retire_catalog_entry` |
| **Actions and events**: elements bound to plugin operations; events handled and components updated | `json_render`: `list_actions`; `web_ui`: `render_page`, `handle_event`, `update_component` |
| **Renderers** | `json_render`: `list_renderers`, `list_packages`; web renderer: json-render's Svelte renderer in 3tched.com |

Rules that carry over unchanged: every visible element is declared in the
catalog; specs are validated before they are shown; the plugin is the schema.

**The generator is proven** (owner, 2026-10-28): it did this job well before
any compliance layer existed. Reuse it as is. Do not rebuild generation,
validation or the catalog; the new work is only the team chat renderer target, the
five governance components (2.3), and routing every action through
compliance, policy and enforcement (2.2).

## 2. What the drop-in adds (new)

### 2.1 Renderer targets

One spec, several targets. A target renders the catalog components it
supports and degrades the rest predictably (never drops an action or a
refusal silently).

| Target | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Web (Svelte) | existing | reference renderer |
| **team chat** (Matrix message) | new — first | messages, modals, interactive buttons |
| Teams (Adaptive Cards), email (HTML) | new — later | same mapping approach |

Component → team chat mapping (initial):

| Catalog component | Matrix messages (HTML + reactions/buttons via widgets) |
|---|---|
| heading, text | `header`, `section` (mrkdwn) |
| key/value facts | `section` with `fields` |
| list, table (small) | `section` lines; large tables → attached file + summary |
| button / action | `actions` with `button` (value = action id) |
| select, input | modal with `static_select` / `plain_text_input` |
| status / progress | `context` line with state |
| **receipt** (new) | `context`: operation id, outcome, capability, event hash |
| **refusal** (new) | `section` with the exact missing capability and the rule that refused |
| **approval request** (new) | `actions` Approve / Reject, shows approvals so far (e.g. 1 of 2) |
| **redaction notice** (new) | `context`: what was redacted and which policy did it |

### 2.2 Governed actions

Every action, on every target, takes one path:

```
user action (web click / team chat button / team chat command)
  → consumer adapter (identifies the user; no authority of its own)
  → compliance router: request → OSCAL controls → candidate plugin operations
  → policy engine: allow / refuse (with reason) / needs approval (n of m)
  → enforcement: the operation runs through the identity's 3tchedFS call file;
    the bridge checks the exact capability and commits
  → result + receipt rendered back on the same target
```

- The adapter never calls plugins directly and never holds grants.
- A refusal is a first-class result, rendered with the missing capability and
  the rule.
- Approvals are collected on the target (chat buttons) and counted by the
  policy engine; root actions need two different humans.
- Redaction is applied by policy before content reaches any target; the
  receipt records it.

### 2.3 New catalog components

`receipt`, `refusal`, `approval_request`, `redaction_notice`, `policy_decision`.
They are declared in the catalog like every other component (web and team chat
renderers both implement them).

### 2.4 Generation stays the same

The model (Meta's) still writes specs from the catalog surface; the spec is
validated before rendering on any target. A target-capability filter keeps the
model to components the destination supports.

## 3. Consumer adapters (new)

| Adapter | Inbound | Outbound | Identity of the user |
|---|---|---|---|
| team chat | slash command, app mention, button, modal submit (outbound client connection to the homeserver: no public inbound URL) | Matrix message messages in thread | chat user mapped to a 3tched principal; unmapped users get read-only answers |

Adapters are thin: parse the event, look up the principal, hand the request to
the router, render the reply. All decisions happen in routing, policy and
enforcement, so every surface behaves identically.

## 4. Acceptance criteria (the working product)

1. A spec that renders on the web renders in team chat with the same actions.
2. From team chat, an allowed request runs through the identity and the thread
   shows the result and its receipt (operation id, outcome).
3. An out-of-bounds request is refused in team chat with the exact missing
   capability and the rule.
4. A root-level request shows an approval request and runs only after two
   different humans approve.
5. Content with PII posted through the drop-in is redacted before display,
   with a redaction notice and receipt.
6. The model (Meta) generates a spec from the catalog; invalid specs are
   rejected before rendering.

## 5. Out of scope

New UI frameworks (web stays Svelte + json-render), direct plugin calls from
adapters, adapters holding grants, a second policy engine per target.

## 6. Generated backends (owner direction, 2026-10-28)

The system does not adopt an existing CMS. It **references** them (Payload,
Strapi, Wagtail, Ghost, Decap) as a feature checklist and data-model source —
content types and fields, relations, roles, draft/review/publish, versioning,
media, webhooks — and **generates its own backend**:

- A generated CMS is a 3tched-native definition: content types are schemas,
  promoted to a sealed plugin; content lives in Cozo through MutationEngine;
  every create/edit/publish is a receipted mutation; policy, redaction and
  approvals apply at write time; the UI comes from the existing generator.
- **The model generates definitions, never backend code.** From a business
  declaration and the reference feature set, Meta's model produces content
  types, fields, roles, workflows and policies; the definition is validated
  against a fixed meta-schema (like UI specs against the catalog).
- **Fixed, tested code** implements CRUD, publish, versioning, redaction and
  receipts once, for any valid definition — so no generated backend can carry
  a bug the model invented.

# Runtime

Where things run, how to call the platform, and what the product may open.
State as of 2026-10-28; **proven** = demonstrated, **planned** = to build.

## Two roles, two users

| Role | Linux user | Where | Has |

| **Run** (the governed service: router, policy, enforcement, chat adapter) | `3tched` (uid 1001) — the Hackathon subsidiary | `/home/3tched/Hackathon` | node/npm, python3; the identity mount |

Only `3tched` can act through the subsidiary's mount; `jeremy` gets
`Permission denied` (**proven**). Build as `jeremy`, run as `3tched`.

## Calling the platform (proven)

The subsidiary's operations are files under
`/home/3tched/Hackathon/3tchedfs/operations/<plugin>/<method>/call`.
Open read-write, write the JSON arguments, fsync, read the result from the same
handle. Helper:

```sh
sudo -u 3tched 3tched-callfile \
  /home/3tched/Hackathon/3tchedfs/operations/identity_sled/get_own_identity/call '{}'
```

Each result includes `required_capability`, `operation_id`, chain
`event_id`/`event_hash` and `outcome`; a refusal names the missing capability.
Schemas: `operations/<plugin>/<method>/{input,output}.schema.json`.
Live state files (`plugins/*/value.json`) currently return EIO — use operations.

The mount is supervised by runit `subsidiary-hackathon-3tchedfs` and survives
reboots (**proven**). It acts as identity `b0c777e3…`, which today also holds
**root** grants — keep demo actions to pre-tested operations until a dedicated
low-privilege identity exists (**planned**; blocked on storage repair).

## OpenFlow development (2026-10-28)

- Bridge `etched0`: isolated OVS bridge for the subsidiary (no ports, no
  address, no uplink, fail-mode `secure`). Never touch `ovsbr0` — it carries
  3tched's own networking.
- The subsidiary holds `openflow.read` (**proven**: `get_datapath_health
  {bridge: etched0}` completed). `openflow.write` is withheld until
  `enforcement/` refuses any flow operation whose `bridge` is not `etched0`;
  platform capabilities are not resource-scoped, so this check is ours to
  build (and a good demo of a refusal).

## Process supervision

The host runs **runit** (not systemd). A long-running service is a runit
service directory (`run` script, `log/run` with svlogd), installed under
`/etc/sv/<name>`, enabled by a symlink in `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default`,
controlled with `sudo sv start|stop|status <name>`. Model new units on
`/etc/sv/subsidiary-hackathon-3tchedfs`. Run product services as `3tched`
(`chpst -u 3tched`).

## Network rules

- The **only** service ingress on this host is `10.0.0.2:8090`. The product
  must not open new listening ports to the outside.
- The team-chat adapter connects **outbound** to its homeserver (no inbound
  webhook). A local homeserver for the demo binds to loopback only.
- The identity container (`3tchedCtlChatbot`) has internet-only egress
  (bridge `hackbr0`, ACL `internet-only`) and no network path to 3tched; it
  reaches 3tched only through its mount (**proven**).
- Any network change must be recorded in
  `/srv/git/odbus-verified/docs/src/operations/network.md`.

## Language choices

## Secrets

Never commit keys. Put runtime secrets in a root- or `3tched`-owned file with
mode `0600` (e.g. `/home/3tched/.config/etched/env`) and load them in the

## Logs and receipts

- Service logs: `/var/log/<service>/current` (svlogd).
- The subsidiary mount's log: `/var/log/op-dbus/subsidiary-hackathon-3tchedfs/`.
- Receipts are the evidence: keep `operation_id` and `event_hash` for every

## FILE: `SPARK-BRIEF.md`

# Etched in Schema — brief for Muse Spark

Hackathon: Meta Model API, **Startup Track — judged on a working product**.
Builder: Jeremy Hobson (3tched).

**Scope (owner, 2026-10-28):** the identity/3tched platform predates the
hackathon and is used through its interfaces. The new, judged development is
(1) compliance routing, (2) rule enforcement, (3) policy, and (4) a drop-in
consumer app (team chat first). The UI is optional. See README "Goals" for the
golden path. Sections below about the avatar, CMS demo and on-chain anchoring
are background, not the critical path.
State as of 2026-10-28. Everything marked **proven** was demonstrated on the
host that day; everything else is planned.

## The project in one paragraph

A self-contained 3tched identity — the "twin", the living embodiment of a
3tched subsidiary — turns a business goal into deployed, verified
infrastructure. It acts only through its own typed filesystem (3tchedFS),
every action is authorised against its capabilities and leaves a
tamper-evident receipt, and a Web3 index anchored on-chain lets anyone verify
who did what, under what authority, without trusting the agent or operator.
That link between on-chain artifacts and accountable, authorised actors is the
gap blocking Web3 adoption.

## Proven today

- **Identity container**: `3tchedCtlChatbot` (Incus, pool `3tched`, profile
  `3tched-lungs`), identity session `b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`,
  service principal, persist volume, kept running by runit `chatbot-identity`.
- **First-person operation call**: inside the container, write the plain JSON
  arguments to `/run/mount/3tchedfs/operations/<plugin>/<method>/call` (open
  read-write, write, fsync, read back on the same handle). Example
  `identity_sled/get_own_identity` with `{}` returned the identity, operation
  `51c8f91c-c2f1-4688-a985-fb41684adfff`, chain events 10389/10390, outcome
  completed. The bridge identifies the caller from the kernel peer over the
  lungs Unix socket, checks the exact capability, commits via MutationEngine.
- **Infrastructure operations available to the identity**: `incus/*`
  (create/start/stop/snapshot/devices), `ovsdb_bridge/*` (bridges, ports,
  transact), plus ~70 plugins. Each call is checked against the identity's
  grants.
- **No network path to 3tched**: the twin talks to 3tched only through its FUSE
  mount. Its only network will be the internet (Meta API, blockchain).
- **Chat path**: UI (`http://10.0.0.2:8080`) → door `10.0.0.2:8090` →
  `chat_router.Chat` → zeroclaw router on `127.0.0.1:8084` (protocol
  `zeroclaw.v1`) → model. Every turn receipted.
- **Avatar**: `IdentityAvatar.svelte` speaks a fixed intro script (exact
  wording, no model) and answers spoken or typed questions via the chat path.

## Where things are

| Thing | Path |
|---|---|
| Backend (Rust workspace) | `/srv/git/odbus-verified` — read its `AGENTS.md` and `HANDOFF.md` first |
| UI (SvelteKit + json-render) | `/srv/git/3tched.com` (has uncommitted WIP — do not publish it as-is) |
| UI build actually live | scratch worktree of 3tched.com HEAD + `tched_router`→`chat_router` + avatar |
| This repo | `/srv/git/etched-in-schema` — Web3 index schema, LLC declaration schema |
| Recovered execution tracker | branch `recover/execution-tracker`, worktree `/srv/git/odbus-tracker-recover` (compiles; not deployed) |
| Router config | `/var/lib/tched-router/config.toml` (root; backups `*.bak-20261028-*`) |
| Qdrant | `127.0.0.1:6333` — `repos_specs_docs_voyage_4_lite`, `repos_repomix_voyage_context_4`, `snowball_footprints`, `blockchain_footprints` |

## Rules that must not be broken

- The plugin IS the schema. Backend schemas live only in Rust plugins under
  `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, sealed into blobs. No standalone
  schema files in op-dbus (that is why drafts live in this repo).
- UI is Svelte/SvelteKit + Vite + json-render's Svelte renderer only. Every
  visible element is a catalog component.
- Never edit Cozo directly, never bypass a permission denial, never add or
  remove Btrfs members outside explicit identity provisioning.
- Deployment is `./activate-golden.sh` / `op-release-launch release`
  (btrfs send/receive slots). Never hand-copy binaries onto the host as a deploy.
- One Cargo process at a time; release builds need `CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint"`.
- Tests only when the owner asks.
- Commit and push at the end of every working turn (owner policy, 2026-10-28): public repo `github.com/repr0bated/etched-in-schema`, branch `master`. No turn ends with unpushed work.

## Plan (10 days)

1. OSCAL catalog of 3tched capabilities with a tag taxonomy; component
   definitions for 3–5 plugins (Compliance Trestle is installed: `trestle`).
2. Tag routing: profile → components → plugin operations.
3. Boundary rules compiled into capability grants and budgets (the bridge
   already enforces grants on every call).
4. "Create a CMS for this business": business declaration (start with
   `schema/llc-declaration.schema.json`) → profile → provision via the twin,
   receipts recorded as OSCAL assessment results and anchored on-chain.
5. UI: avatar intro, then "enough about me — here's what I can do for your
   business" (scripted once the business is chosen), vitals and nerve-trace
   views fed by real receipts, OSCAL views.
Golden path (must work three times in a row before any stretch goal):
scripted intro → "create a CMS for this business" from one small declaration
and one OSCAL profile → the twin provisions one or two real things through its
own mount, with a visible nerve trace and receipts → one receipt anchored
on-chain → a judge verifies it themselves.

Out of scope (owner, 2026-10-28): moving the identity between hosts
("astral projection") — no business case. Client acquisition is optional; add
it only if it fits the flow.

## Known open issues

- Meta model not yet wired into the router (no Meta API key on the host;
  Junie reaches Muse Spark through its JetBrains login). Hermes has a `Meta`
  custom provider stub (`HERMES_CUSTOM_META_API_KEY`).
- Router turn costs ~15k tokens (skills bundle removed to halve it). Qwen does
  not reliably emit text tool calls; MCP compact tools are connected
  (`https://10.0.0.2:8090/mcp`) but retrieval answers came back empty.
- Live state reads through the mount (`plugins/*/value.json`) return EIO.
- Next release will fail activation: `notebook-sources-sync` cannot pass its
  30 s check after restart. Fix before releasing.
- Re-key of the core chatbot to the WireGuard server key (session
  `58287215-0136-f7c3-0a02-d51a593b75ef`) has no supported op yet.
- UI overlay on `dashboard-release` is runtime-only; lost on reboot or release.

## CMS: compliant by construction (owner direction, 2026-10-28)

The CMS is the showcase because it comes out usable *and* evidently
controlled. Pick a handful of controls whose effect is visible on stage; each
control → a CMS behaviour → evidence (receipt or anchor):

| Control area | Visible behaviour | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| PII handling (NIST 800-53 PT) | automatic redaction on publish; original kept only in the owner's private scope | redaction operation receipt naming the triggering policy |
| Audit (AU) | every create/edit/publish attributable | receipt chain: who, capability, when |
| Access control (AC) | roles compiled into capability grants | a live denial showing the exact missing capability |
| Retention (SI-12) | scheduled expiry/archive | scheduled operation receipt |
| Integrity | published versions hash-anchored | on-chain anchor a judge can check |

Pitch wording: "implements and evidences these controls" — never "compliant"
or "certified" (an assessor declares compliance).

## Remote identities: established design (owner, 2026-10-28)

WireGuard is only the establishment step: the peer key proves the identity
once, the decoy issues the signed peer proof (OIA1) and the session gets its
sealed credential (SID1). After that it is zero trust — every call carries the
credential and the door's interceptor re-verifies it, over any transport
(internet, Cloudflare). 3tched-fs `Credential` mode is the remote form of the
lungs. The mechanism exists; it needs testing and refinement, not a rebuild.
Do not add a mesh (Netmaker/Cloudflare) as an identity layer.

# 3tched resources available to the project

These already exist in 3tched (`/srv/git/odbus-verified`, live on the host)
and are used through their interfaces. Status as of 2026-10-28.

## The identity and its mount

- **Identity container** `3tchedCtlChatbot` — session
  `b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`, Incus pool `3tched`, profile
  `3tched-lungs`, persist volume, kept up by runit `chatbot-identity`. **Proven.**
- **3tchedFS mount** inside it at `/run/mount/3tchedfs` (and the threetched
  view at `/run/mount/threetched`), served over the lungs Unix socket
  `/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock` (in-guest symlink `/run/3tched-lungs.socket`).
- Layout: `plugins/<id>/` (schema, capabilities, object metadata),
  `operations/<plugin>/<method>/{call,metadata.json,input.schema.json,output.schema.json}`,
  `capabilities/`, `relationships/`, `view.json`.

### Calling an operation (proven)

Open the method's `call` file read-write, write the plain JSON arguments,
flush (fsync), then read the result from the same handle:

```python
import os
fd = os.open("/run/mount/3tchedfs/operations/identity_sled/get_own_identity/call", os.O_RDWR)
os.write(fd, b"{}")
try: os.fsync(fd)
except OSError: pass
os.lseek(fd, 0, 0)
print(os.read(fd, 200000).decode())
```

The result carries `required_capability`, `operation_id`, chain
`event_id`/`event_hash`, `outcome`. A missing grant is refused with the exact
capability name. Live state reads (`plugins/*/value.json`) currently return
EIO — use operations.

## Plugins (sealed catalog, 72 blobs)

Most relevant to this project:

| Area | Plugins |
|---|---|
| Identity | `identity_sled`, `human_principal`, `keypair`, `users` (create/modify/delete/list Linux users), `persona` |
| Compliance & tags | `oscal_subid_registry` (register, lookup, resolve, export, list_by_category, assess_fields), `schema_tag_registry` (tags, owner-scoped policies, protected-method markers), `routing_decision` |
| Network | `openflow` (add/modify/delete flows, controller, fail mode, datapath health), `ovsdb_bridge` (bridges, ports, transact), `rovs_commands`, `rtnetlink`, `privacy_routes`, `wireguard`, `wg_opdbus` |
| Compute & storage | `incus` (create/start/stop/snapshot instances, devices), `btrfs`, `service`, `packagekit` |
| Knowledge | `qdrant`, `cozo`, `cognitive`, `memory`, `embedding_model`, `snowball` |
| Chat & models | `chat_router` (`Chat`, catalog model binding, generation jobs, config), `chat_response`, `ctl_plane_chatbot`, `model_registry`, `large_language_model` |
| Messaging | `emqx` (topics: `opdbus/wake/<owner-key>`, `opdbus/responder-wake/<key>`, `opdbus/toolsets`, `opdbus/ack/<owner-key>`) |
| UI | `json_render`, `schema_renderer`, `web_ui` |
| Workflow | `workflows`, `cron`, `elevation`, `project` |

Full list: `ls /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/` on the host, or `plugins/` in

## FILE: `docs/SUBSIDIARY-SLED.md`

# Subsidiaries and the identity sled

How an identity works as the embodiment of a subsidiary. Marked **existing**
(in 3tched today), **proven** (demonstrated 2026-10-28) or **planned**.

## Hierarchy (owner model)

- **Root**: the 3tched control plane — the only root on the system. Its chatbot is a one-off part of the
  system core, to be fused with the WireGuard server key so it can never be a
  peer (session `58287215-0136-f7c3-0a02-d51a593b75ef`). **Planned** — no
  supported re-key operation yet.
- **Root has no execution rights**: it holds authority but executes nothing
  itself; execution is delegated through the execution tracker. A human acting
  as root needs **two approvals** (two-person rule). Today `elevation` offers a
  single-use ticket (`authorize_task`, 60 s TTL); the second approval is new
  work. **Planned.**
- **Owner override** (owner requirement): while the owner is the only human,
  his identity must be able to override the two-approval rule. Proposed:
  routine root actions take two approvals from two independent owner devices
  (session + hardware key/phone); an override is break-glass — fresh
  hardware-key confirmation, a cancellable delay, a receipt anchored on-chain,
  and a notification on a second channel — so even the owner cannot act as
  root silently. A designated human second approver replaces this later.
  **Planned.**
- **Second approver = the control-plane chatbot** (owner decision): it co-signs
  the owner's root actions **by policy, not persuasion** — it receives only a
  structured request (operation, resource, identity, applicable policy), never
  free-text justification; atomic judgments (the chatbot or Jev) feed code that
  decides approve/refuse; anything outside written policy is refused and only
  break-glass can override; every decision is receipted with its reasons. It
  approves but never executes. Tiers: routine = owner + chatbot within policy;
  out of policy = refused, break-glass only; later = human second approver.
  **Planned.**
- **Subsidiaries**: Linux users on the system. Each subsidiary is bounded by
  its home directory. **Planned.**
- **Hackathon subsidiary**: embodied by identity `b0c777e3…` (today's
  `3tchedCtlChatbot`). **Existing.**

## What the sled is (existing)

The sled is the identity. For each identity session it holds:

| Part | What it is |
|---|---|
| Record | session id, WireGuard public key, principal kind, genesis hash, trace id, schema version, active flag, timestamps |
| Instance binding | the container that embodies it (name, native UUID, pool) |
| Private leaf | the identity's writable storage, with the canonical subvolumes `@agent_soul`, `@agent_memory`, `@agent_rules`, `@agent_skills`, `@agent_user`, `@agent_shared` (shared/soul read-only; memory/rules/skills/user writable) |
| Session ledger | session events and receipts; the input for vectorization |

Session and principal ids are derived from the public key
(`op-identity::session::derive_session_id` / `derive_principal_id`, Blake3
KDF), so the key, genesis and chain *are* the identity — not a machine.

Lifecycle rules (existing): the identity subsystem owns minting; Cozo owns
assignment; login/start/stop never add or remove Btrfs members; the bridge
only verifies externally mounted storage. Never edit sled rows directly.

## How a subsidiary acts

1. The subsidiary's identity runs in its own container with a 3tchedFS mount
   (lungs). **Proven** for `b0c777e3`.
2. On the host, the same identity's mount is exposed inside the
   subsidiary's home, e.g. `/home/<user>/<Subsidiary>/3tchedfs` and
   `/home/<user>/<Subsidiary>/threetched`, bound to that session
   (`--lungs-session`) with call files owned by that Linux user only
   (call-owner UID). Other users can read schemas but cannot act. **Planned.**
3. Every call: kernel or credential identifies the identity → bridge checks the
   exact capability → MutationEngine commits → receipt. **Proven.**
4. threetched (model/agent) operations used by a subsidiary are its own:
   one router agent per subsidiary with its own model, tool set and budget
   (`max_actions_per_hour`, `max_cost_per_day_cents`). **Planned.**

## Sled + execution tracker (planned)

Every tool call is validated by the one shared execution tracker and written
to the identity's sled session ledger; that ledger is vectorized (Qdrant) so
the identity can answer questions about its own history. Code: branch
`recover/execution-tracker` (`identity_sled_dispatch::subscribe_execution_tracker`).

## Sled + Web3 (planned)

- The index's first entry for an identity records its origin (3tched origin
  session, genesis) and is anchored on-chain.
- A secp256k1 wallet is bound to the identity by a signed link recorded in
  its sled and in the index (the WireGuard key is X25519 and cannot sign
  Ethereum transactions).
- Each index entry references the receipt (`operation_id`, `event_hash`) that
  authorised it.

## Sled + OSCAL boundaries (planned)

The subsidiary's OSCAL profile compiles into: the identity's capability grants
(what it may call), router budgets (how much), and OpenFlow policy on its
network (where it may connect). The bridge already enforces grants on every
call; the new work is generating them from OSCAL.

## FILE: `docs/APPROVALS-SPEC.md`

# Approvals spec: two-approval root, policy co-signer, break-glass

Part of the judged **policy** and **rule enforcement** work. Status: **planned**
(nothing here is built yet). Existing platform pieces are marked **existing**.

## 1. Goal

No root-level action runs on one say-so. Routine root actions need the owner
**and** a policy co-signer (the control-plane chatbot); anything outside
written policy is refused unless the owner uses an audited break-glass path.
Every decision — approve, refuse, override — produces a receipt with reasons.

## 2. Actors

| Actor | Identity | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Owner | human principal `c9bdf32e…`, session `414fbc56…` (existing, containerless) | requests and approves root actions |
| Co-signer | control-plane chatbot (root identity; today `1262e982…`) | approves **by policy only**; never executes |
| Executor | the identity that performs the operation (e.g. the Hackathon subsidiary) | runs the operation after approval, through its mount |
| Later | a designated human second approver | replaces the co-signer for the highest tier |

The root identity holds authority but never executes (owner rule).

## 3. Tiers

| Tier | When | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| **Routine root** | operation is root-level and within written policy | owner approval + co-signer approval |
| **Out of policy** | co-signer finds a policy condition unmet | refused; only break-glass can proceed |
| **Break-glass** | owner overrides a refusal | fresh hardware-key confirmation + cancellable delay + receipt anchored on-chain + second-channel notice |

Non-root operations keep today's behaviour: the bridge's per-call capability
check (**existing**).

## 4. Data model

```text
ApprovalRequest {
  id: uuid                      # request id
  operation: { plugin, method } # e.g. ovsdb_bridge.create_bridge
  arguments_hash: sha256        # of canonical JSON arguments; arguments stored, not free text
  resource: string              # e.g. "bridge:etched0"
  executor: session_id          # identity that will run it
  requested_by: principal_id    # owner
  policy_ref: { profile, control_ids[], version }
  created_at, expires_at        # short TTL (e.g. 10 min)
}

Approval {
  request_id, approver_principal, kind: owner|cosigner|human,
  decision: approve|refuse, reasons[], judgments{}?, receipt: operation_id/event_hash
}

BreakGlass {
  request_id, hardware_key_assertion, delay_s, cancelled: bool,
  anchor: { chain_id, tx | attestation_uid }, notice_channel
}
```

The request is **structured**: the co-signer never sees free-text
justification from the requester.

## 5. Co-signer decision (judgments from the model, decision in code)

The co-signer answers atomic questions about the structured request (the
chatbot via Meta's model, or Jev nouls); **code** decides from fixed
thresholds (yes ≥ 0.7, no ≤ 0.3, otherwise unsettled).

| Judgment (noul) | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `in_declared_boundary` | Is `resource` inside the executor's declared boundary in `policy_ref`? |
| `operation_permitted_by_control` | Does a control in `policy_ref` permit this operation on this resource? |
| `executor_matches_request` | Is the executor the identity the policy assigns to this kind of operation? |
| `destructive` | Would this operation delete or overwrite existing state? |
| `affects_shared_infrastructure` | Does it touch infrastructure other identities depend on (e.g. `ovsbr0`)? |

Truth table (in code):

| in_boundary | permitted | executor_ok | shared_infra | destructive | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | no | any | **approve** |
| yes | yes | yes | yes | any | **refuse** (break-glass only) |
| no or unsettled | — | — | — | — | **refuse** |
| — | no or unsettled | — | — | — | **refuse** |
| — | — | no or unsettled | — | — | **refuse** |

`destructive` does not change the decision; it is recorded and raises the
break-glass delay. Exact-match facts (does `resource` equal an allow-listed
value, is the request expired) are checked in code, not asked of the model.

## 6. Flow

```text
owner request (UI / team chat / mount)
  → build ApprovalRequest (structured; arguments hashed and stored)
  → owner approval (signed by owner session)
  → co-signer: judgments → code decision → Approval + receipt
      approve → issue a single-use execution ticket (existing elevation.authorize_task style, 60 s)
      refuse  → show the reasons; offer break-glass
  → executor runs the operation through its 3tchedFS call file with the ticket;
    the bridge checks the exact capability (existing) → operation receipt
  → result + all receipts shown to the owner
```

Break-glass: owner chooses override → hardware-key assertion (e.g.
FIDO2/WebAuthn) → delay (cancellable from any owner device) → notice on a
second channel → anchor the BreakGlass record on-chain → issue the ticket →
execute as above.

## 7. Enforcement points

- A root-tier operation without a valid ticket (two approvals or break-glass)
  is refused before execution, with the reason.
- Tickets are single-use, bound to `request_id`, `arguments_hash`, `executor`
  and a short TTL; a mismatch is refused.
- The co-signer cannot approve its own requests and holds no execution grants.
- All receipts are append-only; refusals are receipted too.

## 8. Acceptance criteria

1. A routine root action within policy runs only after owner + co-signer
   approval; both approvals and the operation have receipts.
2. A request on a resource outside the boundary (e.g. `bridge:ovsbr0`) is
   refused by the co-signer with the failed judgment named.
3. Free-text added to a request does not change the co-signer's decision
   (test: same structured request ± persuasive text → same decision).
4. Break-glass requires the hardware-key step and the delay, can be cancelled
   during the delay, and leaves an anchored record.
5. Reusing a ticket, changing arguments after approval, or executing after
   expiry is refused.

## 9. Integration with existing 3tched

| Need | Existing piece |
|---|---|
| per-call capability check | bridge admission |
| single-use ticket shape | `elevation.authorize_task` (60 s TTL), `list_protected_actions` |
| receipts | MutationEngine operation ids and chain events |
| identities | owner human session; chatbot service identity; subsidiary identity |
| model judgments | Meta (`META_API_KEY`), TypeSafe Jev (`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`) |

## 10. Open questions

- Hardware key: FIDO2/WebAuthn via the web UI, or a separate device app?
- Where the approval store lives: a new sealed plugin (preferred, receipted) or
  this repo's service with receipts written through the identity.
- Delay length per tier, and the second notification channel.

## FILE: `docs/PRIOR-ART.md`

# Prior art and positioning

How Etched in Schema relates to production identity systems, and what it adds.
Use this for the pitch, the YC application, and design decisions.

## The pattern is proven in production

The remote-identity design (establish once, then zero trust over any
transport) matches **SPIFFE/SPIRE**, the CNCF standard for workload identity:

| 3tched | SPIFFE/SPIRE equivalent |
|---|---|
| Kernel-peer check on the lungs Unix socket | SPIRE Unix workload attestor — identifies the calling process over a Unix socket using kernel peer credentials (same mechanism) |
| WireGuard key establishes the identity once (decoy issues OIA1, session gets SID1) | Node attestation: the machine proves itself once (cloud identity document, TPM, join token) |
| Sealed credential (SID1), then zero trust over any transport | Short-lived SVIDs (X.509/JWT) verified on every connection (mutual TLS) |
| Door interceptor re-verifies every call | Each service verifies the peer's SVID per request |

Other production relatives:

- **Google BeyondCorp, Cloudflare Access** — zero trust: nothing is trusted for
  being on the network; every request is verified against identity and policy.
- **AWS IAM Roles Anywhere, cloud instance identity** — a workload proves
  itself once, then uses short-lived credentials from anywhere.
- **W3C DIDs and Verifiable Credentials** — the standard for portable,
  self-controlled identity anyone can verify; the Web3-adjacent reference.

## What 3tched adds (the differentiators)

1. **The identity is the entity, not a label.** SPIFFE names a workload whose
   state and history live elsewhere. In 3tched the identity *is* the key,
   genesis and receipt chain, with its own container, memory and storage.
2. **Capability per typed operation.** SPIFFE answers "who is this?" and leaves
   "what may it do?" to each service. 3tched checks the exact capability for
   each schema-declared operation centrally and records a receipt.
3. **Verifiable history.** Workload identity proves who is calling now. 3tched
   adds a tamper-evident record of everything the identity has done,
   anchorable on-chain.
4. **Compliance by construction.** OSCAL requirements compile into the grants,
   budgets and network policy that are actually enforced, with receipts as the
   assessment evidence.

## Transport and identity (decided)

- WireGuard is only the establishment step; after that the credential carries
  identity over any transport. The mechanism exists; it needs testing and
  refinement.
- **Netmaker** (WireGuard mesh) would only add connectivity; it is retired from
  3tched and not needed.
- **Cloudflare** (WARP/mesh) is acceptable as a pipe, never as the identity
  layer: devices authenticate to Cloudflare with Cloudflare's keys, so the
  bridge would see a Cloudflare address, not the identity's key. Identity stays
  proven end to end by the credential.
- Sealed blobs (schemas) are content-addressed: they travel with the identity
  or are fetched by hash over any channel and verified.
- What the model depends on: credential binding to the key, expiry,
  revocation, and replay refusal. Known gap (HANDOFF, 2026-09-25): the
  interceptor still mints genesis server-side when no session exists, and the
  decoy mints only OIA1 — verify before relying on remote identities.

## Pitch lines

- *"Workload identity like SPIFFE proves who is calling. Etched in Schema also
  proves what the identity was allowed to do — and what it actually did."*
- *"Every on-chain thing the agent creates comes with a verifiable answer to
  who did it, what they were allowed to do, and what really happened."*
- *"Implements and evidences these controls"* — never "compliant" or
  "certified".

# How to win this hackathon

Ten priorities for the demo and submission. When in doubt, choose whatever
makes the golden path more reliable or more verifiable.

1. **Unforgettable first 30 seconds.** The avatar speaks the exact intro
   script, then immediately does one real thing, with its receipt appearing on
   screen. Show proof before explaining anything.

2. **Let a judge verify something themselves.** Hand them a receipt ID or
   on-chain anchor and a one-step way to check it (link or QR code). "Don't
   trust me, check it" is the thesis made physical.

3. **Show one refusal live.** Ask the identity to do something outside its
   OSCAL boundary; the bridge refuses with the exact missing capability. An
   agent that *can't* misbehave beats one that doesn't.

4. **Use Meta's model visibly and well.** Show Muse Spark doing the reasoning
   (planning the business, mapping requirements to controls), say so on
   screen, and let it make one real tool call through the identity's mount.

5. **Protect the golden path above everything.** Intro → "create a CMS for this
   business" → provision → receipts → anchor. Run it end to end daily from
   Day 5. If it does not pass three times in a row, add nothing new.

6. **Redaction is the "wow" moment.** Content with a name, email and phone
   number is published and masked automatically, with the receipt naming the
   policy. Everyone understands it instantly.

7. **A fallback for every live dependency.** Record a full run and know the
   exact step at which you would switch to it. Model, chain or Wi-Fi can fail
   on stage; a calm switch still scores.

8. **Tell a story with a real business.** One believable small business (e.g.
   a Fort Lauderdale firm that needs a compliant client portal), with a name
   and a problem, solved by the identity.

9. **Say the positioning line out loud.** *"Workload identity like SPIFFE
   proves who is calling. Etched in Schema also proves what it was allowed to
   do — and what it actually did."*

10. **Ship the evidence, not just the demo.** Public repo with a README that
    separates new from pre-existing work, a short video, a one-page
    architecture diagram, and a live link judges can open later.

**Bonus: freeze scope on Day 7.** After that, only polish, rehearse and fix.

## FILE: `review/out/findings.md`

# Jev strategy review (jev-1.14.0, 2026-10-28)

Jev answered atomic questions about the strategy state in `review/jev_strategy.py`; the findings below are decided in code from fixed thresholds (yes ≥ 0.7, no ≤ 0.3).

- Scope fit: 1.98 on 0 (fits) … 2 (clearly over-scoped), probabilities {'0': 0.0, '1': 0.01, '2': 0.99}.
- Overall judge appeal: 1.39 on 0 (familiar) … 2 (novel, clearly demonstrated), probabilities {'0': 0.05, '1': 0.51, '2': 0.44} — split between 'interesting' and 'stand-out'.

## Findings (decided in code)
- (unsettled) Rewrite the thesis in plain words for non-specialists. — `judge.thesis_clear` = 0.32
- **Cut the concepts shown in the demo to the three that carry the thesis.** — `judge.concept_overload` = 0.97
- **Most of the golden path is unproven: prove it end to end before adding scope.** — `feas.path_mostly_proven` = 0.12
- **The golden path depends on open issues: fix those first.** — `feas.path_depends_on_open_issue` = 0.94
- **Get Meta's model wired in first; it is a hard requirement.** — `feas.meta_blocker` = 0.95
- **De-risk tool calling: test it early with Meta's model or move tool calls into code.** — `feas.tool_calling_risk` = 0.97
- **Stabilise the platform: commit often, fix the activation health check, make the UI part of a release.** — `feas.platform_unstable` = 0.97
- **Record a full fallback run as soon as the golden path first works.** — `feas.fallback_ready` = 0.02
- **Do not demo with root: use a dedicated low-privilege identity or restrict the demo to pre-tested operations.** — `sec.demo_overprivileged` = 0.98
- **Prove on-chain anchoring early; it is the verification claim.** — `sec.anchoring_proven` = 0.16
- **Name a first customer (even a design partner) for the pitch and YC.** — `biz.first_customer_named` = 0.03
- **State a revenue model for YC.** — `biz.revenue_stated` = 0.03
- **Lead with verifiability and compliance; present the blockchain as the neutral witness, not the product.** — `biz.web3_may_deter_enterprise` = 0.85

|---|---|---|---|

## FILE: `schema/index-entry.schema.json`

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://3tched.com/schema/etched-index-entry/v1",
  "title": "EtchedIndexEntry",
  "description": "One thing an identity created or did in Web3, linked to the 3tched receipt that authorised and recorded it.",
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": ["format", "seq", "prev_hash", "kind", "artifact", "identity", "receipt", "created_at"],
  "properties": {
    "format": { "const": "etched.index-entry/1" },
    "seq": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "description": "Position in this identity's append-only index." },
    "prev_hash": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$", "description": "sha256 of the previous entry's canonical JSON; 64 zeros for seq 0." },
    "kind": { "enum": ["contract", "token", "attestation", "ipfs_object", "domain", "offer", "transaction", "other"] },
    "artifact": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["ref"],
      "properties": {
        "chain_id": { "type": "integer", "description": "EIP-155 chain id, e.g. 84532 for Base Sepolia." },
        "ref": { "type": "string", "description": "Transaction hash, contract address, CID, or URL." },
        "description": { "type": "string", "maxLength": 500 }
      }
    },
    "identity": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["session_id", "genesis"],
      "properties": {
        "session_id": { "type": "string", "format": "uuid" },
        "genesis": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{64}$" },
        "origin_session_id": { "type": "string", "format": "uuid", "description": "The 3tched identity this twin branched from." }
      }
    },
    "receipt": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["operation_id", "event_hash", "plugin", "method"],
      "properties": {
        "operation_id": { "type": "string", "format": "uuid" },
        "event_hash": { "type": "string" },
        "plugin": { "type": "string" },
        "method": { "type": "string" },
        "required_capability": { "type": "string" }
      }
    },
    "resource": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "properties": {
        "gas_used": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 },
        "cost_usd_micros": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }
      }
    },
    "created_at": { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" }
  }
}
```
